about: DRAFT, never run. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL 120B-A12B, ggml-org's GGUF conversion of NVIDIA's QAD NVFP4 checkpoint (AA index within 0.1 of BF16), with the Q8_0 image projector and the NVFP4 LiLiCorr drafter from the same repository (draft-dflash, 7 tokens). vLLM can't serve it here: NVIDIA's DGX Spark recipe needs vLLM 0.32 and --gpu-memory-utilization 0.75 for the 75 GB checkpoint, past the N1X's practical 0.6. Upstream llama.cpp b11718 (CUDA 13.4.1, native NVFP4 W4A4 on Blackwell). 88 layers, only 8 attention (2 KV heads x 128), so the KV is 8 KB a token: 131,072 tokens is 1 GiB bf16, q8_0 halves it. 79.2 GB (73.8 GiB) of weights leave ~11 GiB for KV, Mamba state, compute buffers and the drafter under a ~85 GiB budget; ubatch 1024 keeps the compute buffer down. If it does not fit beside the desktop, the fallback is unsloth UD-Q3_K_XL (65.76 GB, 75a58290) with the same flags.
setup: One RTX Spark N1X with ~80 GiB MemAvailable at start (close the browser first; watch MemAvailable with the memwatch script and stop below ~8 GiB). ~79 GB of downloads (76.92 GB NVFP4 GGUF + 0.97 GB mmproj + 1.35 GB LiLiCorr). No measured Spark speed published yet; the older Nemotron 3 Super did 19.5 tok/s on a DGX Spark in llama.cpp Q4_K, so expect ~20 tok/s without drafts and more with LiLiCorr.
